newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty condemns torture of Turkish children.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty condemns torture of Turkish children.

text.p: Amnesty International condemned on Wednesday the torture of children held in custody in Turkey and urged the government in Ankara to abide by the Convention on the Rights of the Child which it signed last year.

The London-based human rights group said in a report that children as young as 12, in some cases detained on suspicion of minor offences, "had been subjected to appalling cruelty in police custody," including beatings and electric shocks.
In a 31-page report it documented cases of children who had died or disappeared in police custody over the past four years.
In Ankara, a Turkish foreign ministry spokesman rejected the allegations of child torture and said Amnesty was part of a campaign to sully Turkey's image internationally.
"This subject is being exploited in some circles through defamatory campaigns against Turkey," ministry spokesman Omer Akbel told reporters at a regular news briefing.

"Our country has signed and put into effect the children's rights agreement," he said. "Work on harmonising with international standards is carried out, regularly taking into account regulations connected with children."

Amnesty gave the example of a trial that ended in October of two police officers accused of kicking and clubbing 12-year-old Halil Ibrahim Okkali in a police station in Izmir. The child was sent to intensive care. The officers were found guilty of ill-treatment and fined the equivalent of $8, Amnesty said.

Amnesty accused the Turkish security forces as well as the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) of being responsible for the death of children in southeast Turkey where the Kurdish group is fighting for self-rule.
